examples.en: I hurt my leg, so I get around on crutches.
Stairs are hard because of the crutches.
I'm happy that I can walk without crutches now.
My friend came to school on crutches.
I learned how to use crutches at the hospital.

examples.ko: 목발을 짚은 사람에게 문을 잡아 줬어요.
examples.en: I held the door for a person on crutches.

explain: 다리가 아파서 걸을 때 겨드랑이에 끼고 짚는 지팡이예요. '목발을 짚다', '목발을 쓰다'처럼 말해요. 손으로 잡는 '지팡이'와는 다르게 몸을 받쳐 주는 도구로 생각하면 돼요.

phrases.example: 이제 목발 없이 걸을 수 있어요.
phrases.en: I can walk without crutches now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다리가 나아서 목발을 쓰지 않게 됐을 때 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a leg has healed and you no longer need crutches.

phrases.en: My friend walks slowly on crutches.
phrases.nuance_ko: '짚다'에 '걷다'를 이어서 걷는 모습을 구체적으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 걷다 after 짚다 describes the way someone is walking.

phrases.en: I borrowed crutches from the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잠깐 필요해서 사지 않고 빌릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you only need crutches for a short time and borrow instead of buying.

explain_en: These are the sticks you tuck under your arms and lean on when walking with an injured leg. You say '목발을 짚다' or '목발을 쓰다'. Unlike a '지팡이' (cane) held in the hand, think of them as a tool that supports your body weight.

examples.ko: 새 신발을 신었더니 발에 물집이 생겼어요.
examples.en: I wore new shoes and got a blister on my foot.

examples.ko: 뜨거운 물에 데어서 손에 물집이 났어요.
examples.en: I got scalded by hot water and a blister came up on my hand.

examples.ko: 물집은 억지로 터뜨리지 않는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's best not to pop a blister by force.

examples.ko: 등산 때문에 발바닥 물집이 아파서 쉬었어요.
examples.en: The blister on my sole hurt from hiking, so I rested.
I put a bandage on the blister and kept walking.

examples.ko: 오랫동안 삽질을 했더니 손에 물집이 잡혔어요.
examples.en: After shoveling for a long time, blisters formed on my hands.

explain: 물집은 '생기다, 잡히다, 터지다'처럼 같이 쓰는 동사가 많고, '물집이 잡혔다'는 말도 자주 들어요. 피부가 쓸리거나 데면 생겨요. 피부 밑에서 피가 나 색이 변하는 '멍'과는 달라요.

phrases.en: After walking a long time, I got a blister on my foot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물집이 처음 만들어졌을 때 가장 기본으로 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic phrase for when a blister first forms.

phrases.en: The blister burst and it hurt a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물집 속 물이 나올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the fluid inside the blister comes out.

phrases.en: A blister formed on my palm.
phrases.nuance_ko: '생기다'와 비슷하지만 쓸리거나 눌려서 생긴 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 생기다, but it suggests the blister came from rubbing or pressure.

explain_en: 물집 goes with many verbs, such as 생기다, 잡히다 and 터지다, and 물집이 잡혔다 is a very common phrase. It forms when skin is rubbed or burned. It differs from 멍 (a bruise), where blood under the skin changes its color.

examples.en: My child had a slight fever, so he stayed home from school.
I have a mild fever, but I'm not badly sick.
My body feels sluggish because of a slight fever.
When I took my temperature, it was only a slight fever.
A mild fever and a cough have continued for days.
In the evening I feel weak from a mild fever.

explain: 몸이 조금 뜨거운 정도의 약한 열이에요. 반대로 높은 열은 '고열'이라고 해요. 병원에서는 '미열이 있다', '미열이 나다'처럼 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: I've had a slight fever since yesterday, so I took medicine.
phrases.nuance_ko: '미열이 있다'가 상태라면 '미열이 나다'는 열이 생기기 시작한 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: '미열이 나다' stresses that the fever has just started, while '있다' states the condition.

phrases.en: The slight fever has continued for two days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 열이 오래 이어질 때 써요. 병원에서 증상을 설명할 때 좋아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when a mild fever lasts. Handy for describing symptoms at a clinic.

phrases.en: I have mild fever symptoms because of a cold.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기침, 두통처럼 다른 증상과 함께 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used alongside other symptoms like cough or headache.

explain_en: It is a low-grade fever where the body is only a little warm. A high fever is '고열'. At the doctor's it is said as '미열이 있다' or '미열이 나다'.

examples.ko: 아이가 제 바짓가랑이를 붙잡고 놓지 않아요.
examples.en: The child is holding on to my pant leg and won't let go.
My pant legs got completely wet because of the rain.
I rolled up my pant legs and stepped into the stream.
Your pant legs are covered in dirt.
The excited puppy kept tugging at my pant leg with its teeth.
The pant legs are so long that I keep stepping on them.

explain: 바지에서 한쪽 다리가 들어가는 부분이에요. 아이가 매달리거나 비에 젖는 장면에서 자주 나와요. 줄여서 '가랑이'라고도 하지만 몸의 다리 사이를 가리킬 수도 있어서, 옷 이야기에서는 '바짓가랑이'가 더 분명해요.

phrases.example: 취직 좀 시켜 달라고 사장님 바짓가랑이를 붙잡고 늘어졌어요.
phrases.en: I clung to the boss's pant leg and begged him to give me a job.
phrases.nuance_ko: 체면을 가리지 않고 끈질기게 부탁하거나 매달릴 때 쓰는 비유예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figure of speech for begging or clinging on persistently without caring about dignity.
phrases.en_equiv: to cling to someone and beg; to hang on and plead

explain_en: It is the part of the pants that covers one leg, and it often appears when a child clings on or the pants get wet. It can be shortened to '가랑이', but that can also mean the crotch of the body, so '바짓가랑이' is clearer when talking about clothes.

examples.en: The child has cough and fever symptoms.
They check for fever at the entrance.
If the fever continues, go to the hospital.
Even after taking medicine, the fever won't go down.
The battery shut off because of overheating.
Patients with a fever, please wait separately.

explain: 몸이나 기계에서 열이 나는 것을 말하는 딱딱한 말이에요. 일상에서 사람이 아플 때는 '열이 나요'라고 하고, 병원이나 안내문에서 '발열'을 써요. 기계에는 '과열'(너무 뜨거워짐)을 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 아이가 밤에 열이 나서 병원에 갔어요.
phrases.en: My child had a fever at night, so we went to the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: '발열'의 일상적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The everyday way to say '발열'.

phrases.en: I've had a fever since yesterday, so I took medicine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원이나 안내문처럼 조금 딱딱한 자리에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in slightly formal places like clinics and notices.

phrases.en: This vest has a heating function.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 아니라 옷이나 기계에서 열이 나는 기능을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to heat from clothes or machines, not from a person.

explain_en: Giving off heat; fever symptom or technical term for reactions. It is a formal word for giving off heat, from a body or from a machine. In daily speech you say 열이 나요 when you are sick; 발열 appears in hospitals and notices. For machines that get too hot, 과열 is the common word.

t90.ax: They check for fever at the entrance.

examples.ko: 라면을 먹고 잤더니 얼굴에 부기가 있어요.
examples.en: I ate ramen and slept, so my face is puffy.

examples.ko: 발목을 삐어서 부기가 아직 안 빠졌어요.
examples.en: I sprained my ankle and the swelling hasn't gone down yet.

examples.ko: 얼음찜질을 하면 부기를 줄일 수 있어요.
examples.en: An ice pack can reduce swelling.
Every morning I worry about puffy eyes.

examples.ko: 수술한 뒤 일주일 동안 부기가 심했어요.
examples.en: For a week after the surgery, the swelling was severe.

examples.ko: 부기를 빼려고 물을 많이 마시고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm drinking lots of water to get rid of the puffiness.

explain: 몸이 붓는 것을 말하고, '부기가 빠지다', '부기를 빼다'처럼 동사와 함께 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '붓기'라고도 많이 해요. 같은 소리의 '부기(장부 적기)'는 다른 말이에요.

phrases.en: My eyes are puffy when I wake up.
phrases.nuance_ko: '부기'와 뜻이 같고, 일상 대화에서는 '붓기'를 더 많이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 부기; 붓기 is more common in everyday speech.

phrases.en: The swelling went down after I used an ice pack.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부은 곳이 가라앉을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common collocation for swelling going down.

phrases.en: I exercise every morning to reduce puffiness.
phrases.nuance_ko: '부기가 빠지다'와 달리 내가 일부러 부기를 줄일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Unlike 부기가 빠지다, this means you actively reduce the swelling.

explain_en: It means swelling of the body, used as 부기가 빠지다 or 부기를 빼다. In daily talk people also say 붓기. There is another 부기 (bookkeeping) with the same sound, but it is a different word.

examples.en: Since yesterday, pimples have come up on my forehead and chin.

examples.ko: 뾰루지를 손으로 짜면 흉터가 남을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you squeeze a pimple with your hands, it can leave a scar.

examples.ko: 이마에 난 뾰루지 때문에 앞머리로 가렸어요.
examples.en: I covered the pimple on my forehead with my bangs.
A pimple usually goes down after a few days.
I bought an ointment for pimples at the pharmacy.
I don't have acne, but I get pimples sometimes.

explain: '뾰루지가 나다'라고 말해요. 여드름과 비슷하지만 피곤하거나 피부가 예민할 때 갑자기 생긴 것에도 넓게 쓰는 말이에요.

phrases.en: When I am tired, a pimple appears on my forehead.
phrases.nuance_ko: '나다'와 같은 뜻으로, 새로 올라온 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 나다, used for a new pimple appearing.

phrases.en: Do not squeeze the pimple; put medicine on it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손으로 눌러서 터뜨리는 동작을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes pressing a pimple with your hands to pop it.

phrases.en: During puberty, many pimples come out on the face.
phrases.nuance_ko: '뾰루지'보다 더 흔히 반복해서 나는 피부 트러블을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the more common, recurring kind of skin trouble.

explain_en: You say '뾰루지가 나다'. It is similar to acne, but it is a broad word that also covers bumps that suddenly appear when you are tired or your skin is sensitive.

examples.en: My wisdom tooth is coming in and my gums hurt.
Yesterday I went to the dentist and had my wisdom tooth pulled.

examples.ko: 사랑니를 뽑고 나서 하루 종일 죽만 먹었어요.
examples.en: After getting my wisdom tooth pulled, I only ate porridge all day.

examples.ko: 사랑니는 어른이 되어서 나는 경우가 많아요.
examples.en: Wisdom teeth often come in once you're an adult.
I heard my lower wisdom tooth grew in at a slant.
It's hard to eat because of my wisdom tooth.

explain: '사랑니가 나다', '사랑니를 뽑다'가 가장 자주 쓰는 짝이에요. 치과에서는 '사랑니 발치'라고도 해요. 영어의 wisdom tooth처럼 '지혜'가 아니라 '사랑'이라는 말이 들어가서 재미있게 외울 수 있어요.

phrases.en: My wisdom tooth has been hurting for a few days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사랑니 때문에 통증이 있을 때 쓰는 가장 쉬운 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The simplest way to say a wisdom tooth is causing pain.

phrases.en: I decided to have my wisdom tooth pulled next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: '뽑다'와 같은 뜻으로, 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 뽑다, and common in speech.
phrases.en_equiv: to have a wisdom tooth pulled

phrases.example: 사랑니 발치 후에는 이틀 정도 푹 쉬세요.
phrases.en: After wisdom tooth removal, rest well for about two days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 치과에서 쓰는 말이고 조금 딱딱한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The term used at the dentist; it sounds somewhat formal.

explain_en: The most common pairings are '사랑니가 나다' (a wisdom tooth comes in) and '사랑니를 뽑다' (pull a wisdom tooth). At the dentist it's also called '사랑니 발치'. Unlike English 'wisdom', the Korean word has 'love' in it, which makes it fun to remember.

examples.en: My younger sibling has had eczema since childhood.

examples.ko: 겨울에는 아토피 때문에 피부가 많이 가려워요.
examples.en: In winter, my skin gets very itchy because of eczema.

examples.ko: 아토피 피부에는 순한 비누를 쓰는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It is good to use mild soap on eczema-prone skin.
I got treatment for my eczema at the hospital and it improved a lot.

examples.ko: 이 로션은 아토피로 고생하는 아이들에게 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: This lotion is popular with kids who suffer from eczema.
I heard that eczema started after moving into the new house.

explain: '아토피'는 보통 '아토피 피부염'을 줄여서 말해요. 가려움과 건조함이 특징이라 '아토피가 있다', '아토피가 생기다', '아토피가 심하다'처럼 써요. 일상에서는 '습진'보다 '아토피'를 더 자주 들어요.

phrases.en: I go to the hospital because of atopic dermatitis.
phrases.nuance_ko: '아토피'의 정확한 병 이름이라 병원에서 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The full name of the condition, used at the hospital.

phrases.example: 동생은 아토피가 심해서 로션을 자주 발라요.
phrases.en: My younger sibling's atopy is severe, so they put on lotion often.
phrases.nuance_ko: 증상이 많이 나쁠 때 '심하다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '심하다' when the symptoms are bad.

phrases.en: Mild soap is good for atopic skin.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아토피가 있는 피부를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for skin that has atopy.

explain_en: 아토피 is the everyday short form of 아토피 피부염 (atopic dermatitis). People say 아토피가 있다, 아토피가 생기다, or 아토피가 심하다. In daily talk, Koreans hear 아토피 much more often than 습진.

en: to worsen; to become worse; to deteriorate

examples.ko: 날씨가 갑자기 악화해서 비행기가 못 떠요.
examples.en: The weather suddenly worsened, so the plane can't take off.

examples.ko: 병이 악화하지 않도록 약을 꼭 드세요.
examples.en: Take your medicine so the illness doesn't get worse.

examples.ko: 두 나라의 관계가 점점 악화하고 있어요.
examples.en: Relations between the two countries are gradually worsening.

examples.ko: 건강이 악화한 뒤로 일을 쉬고 있어요.
examples.en: Since my health deteriorated, I've been taking a break from work.
If the situation gets worse, contact me right away.
Noise made my relationship with the neighbors worse.

explain: '병이 악화하다', '관계가 악화하다'처럼 주어가 스스로 나빠질 때 써요. 같은 뜻으로 '악화되다'도 쓰고, 누군가 나빠지게 만들 때는 '악화시키다'를 써요. 반대말은 '호전되다'예요.

phrases.en: The weather got worse, so the game was canceled.
phrases.nuance_ko: '악화하다'와 뜻이 같고 일상에서 더 자주 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '악화하다' and more common in daily speech.

phrases.en: Stress makes your health worse.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누가 또는 무엇이 일을 나쁘게 만들 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone or something makes a situation worse.

phrases.example: 두 나라의 관계가 점점 악화하고 있어요.
phrases.en: The relationship between the two countries is getting worse.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이나 나라 사이가 나빠질 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for relationships between people or countries getting worse.

explain_en: It is used when the subject itself gets worse, as in '병이 악화하다' and '관계가 악화하다'. '악화되다' is also used with the same meaning, and '악화시키다' is for someone making things worse. The opposite is '호전되다'.

p.n: The other form is more common in speech.

examples.en: In winter a duck-down jacket is the warmest.

examples.ko: 이 이불은 오리털이 가득 들어 있어요.
examples.en: This blanket is stuffed full of duck down.

examples.ko: 오리털 패딩을 세탁할 때는 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: You have to be careful when washing a duck-down padded coat.
I bought a light, warm duck-down pillow.
Down feathers poked out and made the coat look messy.
Duck down is cheaper than goose down.

explain: 패딩이나 이불 속에 넣는 오리의 부드러운 털이에요. 비슷한 재료로 '거위털(구스다운)'이 있는데, 보통 더 비싸요. 옷 상표에서는 '다운'이라는 말도 같이 봐요.

phrases.en: It's winter, so I bought a down padded jacket.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겨울 옷 이름에 가장 많이 붙는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, used for winter clothes.

phrases.en: A duck down blanket is light and warm.
phrases.nuance_ko: 침구 재료를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say what bedding is filled with.

phrases.en: Down keeps coming out of my old padded jacket.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷 사이로 털이 밖으로 나올 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when feathers poke out through the fabric.

explain_en: It is the soft down of ducks used to fill padded coats and blankets. A similar material is '거위털' (goose down), which is usually pricier. On clothing labels you will also see the word '다운'.

examples.en: If I sit for a long time, I get a backache.
I get physical therapy at the hospital because of back pain.

examples.ko: 아버지는 요통으로 오래 서 있기 힘드세요.
examples.en: My father finds it hard to stand for long because of lower back pain.

examples.ko: 요통에는 가벼운 걷기 운동이 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: Light walking exercise helps with lower back pain.

examples.ko: 요통은 한 번 생기면 오래가기도 해요.
examples.en: Once you get lower back pain, it can sometimes last a long time.
If the back pain continues, get it checked.

explain: 일상에서는 '허리가 아프다', '허리 통증'이라고 많이 말해요. '요통'은 병원이나 건강 정보에서 더 자주 보여요. '허리'는 몸의 부위이고 '요통'은 아픈 증상을 가리켜요.

phrases.en: My backache has been bad since yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아픈 정도를 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase for describing how bad the pain is.

phrases.example: 허리 통증 때문에 오래 걷기 힘들어요.
phrases.en: Because of back pain, it's hard to walk for long.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 '요통' 대신 더 쉽게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler everyday alternative to '요통'.

phrases.en: I'm resting from exercise because of my backache.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원인을 말할 때 쓰는 연결 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connecting phrase for giving a cause.

explain_en: In daily life people more often say '허리가 아프다' or '허리 통증'. '요통' appears more in hospitals and health information. '허리' is the body part, while '요통' refers to the pain symptom.

examples.ko: 날씨가 추우니까 웃옷을 하나 더 입어요.
examples.en: It's cold, so put on one more outer layer.
Take off your jacket and hang it on the chair.
I got rained on, and my jacket is all wet.
This jacket goes well with the pants.
It was hot, so I worked with my outer layer off.
I put the key in my jacket pocket.

explain: 맨 겉에 입는 옷을 말해요. 바지나 치마와 짝이 되는 '윗옷(상의)'과 철자가 달라서 헷갈리기 쉬워요. 일상에서는 '겉옷'이라고도 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: It's cold outside, so wear an outer layer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 더 자주 쓰는 같은 뜻의 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common everyday word with a similar meaning.

phrases.en: I put on an outer jacket and go out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉에 입는 옷을 걸치고 나갈 때 쓰는 기본 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic collocation for putting on outer clothing.

phrases.en: I draped a jacket over my shoulders.
phrases.nuance_ko: 단추를 잠그지 않고 가볍게 입거나 어깨에 얹을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when loosely throwing on a jacket without fastening it.

explain_en: It means the outermost garment you wear. It is easy to confuse with '윗옷' (a top, as opposed to pants or a skirt) because the spelling differs. In daily speech people also often say '겉옷'.

examples.ko: 저는 위장병 때문에 매운 음식을 못 먹어요.
examples.en: I can't eat spicy food because of my stomach trouble.
My father has suffered from a stomach disorder for a long time.

examples.ko: 스트레스가 심하면 위장병이 생길 수 있어요.
examples.en: Heavy stress can cause stomach trouble.
Regular meals are important for stomach trouble.
I took stomach medicine and felt a bit better.
My friend was hospitalized for a stomach disorder.

explain: 위나 장이 오래 안 좋은 상태를 넓게 부르는 말이에요. 병명이 아니라 '위장 쪽 병'이라는 느낌이라서 일상에서 많이 써요. 병원에서는 '위염', '장염'처럼 더 정확한 이름을 말해요.

phrases.en: I have a stomach condition, so I'm careful.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오래된 위장 문제를 말할 때 가장 쉽게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The simplest way to mention a long-standing stomach problem.

phrases.en: When you're stressed, you easily get a stomach disorder.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병이 새로 생겼을 때 '걸리다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 걸리다 is used when an illness newly develops.
phrases.en_equiv: to come down with a stomach disorder

phrases.en: My stomach is bad, so I eat porridge.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병 이름 대신 몸 상태를 부드럽게 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A softer way to describe your condition without naming an illness.

explain_en: It is a broad term for long-term stomach or bowel problems. It is not a precise diagnosis but a general 'stomach-area illness', so it is common in daily talk. Hospitals use more exact names like '위염' or '장염'.
